memory_candidates.content: In this harness/environment, SHELLOPTS (including errexit) is inherited from the invoking shell into every bash subprocess, even when a script's own header only declares `set -uo pipefail` (no `-e`). A plain `var="$(cmd)"` assignment whose RHS command substitution exits non-zero will silently kill the whole script immediately under this inherited errexit, with no visible error -- the script just stops mid-trace. Existing test suites in this codebase defensively wrap any command expected to possibly exit non-zero in `set +e ... cmd ...; rc=$?; set -e 2>/dev/null || true` for exactly this reason. When writing a NEW test case that intentionally exercises a command's non-zero-exit path, always use this wrap, even if the script's own `set` line doesn't mention `-e`.

A corpus-measurement probe whose file enumeration is `git ls-files`-based (for speed and .gitignore-respect) only sees TRACKED files. A newly-created file that has not yet been `git add`-ed is invisible to such a probe and silently undercounts any 'files/lines added' delta until it is staged (or committed). When measuring a phase's net line-count delta for a task with a net-deletion/net-addition acceptance criterion, stage new files with `git add` before trusting the probe's own before/after figure, or measure via direct `wc -l` arithmetic instead, which is unaffected by git tracking state.

When a fixture test suite resolves the tool-under-test via a 'deploy-tree-first, source-store-fallback' convention (checking .claude/scripts/<name>.sh before the source-store copy), any source-store edit will NOT be exercised by that suite until the deployed tree is re-synced via the project's deploy script (here: deploy-headless.sh, default resync mode, non-destructive, ~170s). Running the suite against stale deployed code produces spurious failures (or spurious passes) that look like regressions but are purely a stale-deploy artifact. Re-deploy after each source-store edit to a file covered by such a suite, before trusting a local test run's result.
